claim.quote: Observation of the doubly charmed baryon $\Xi_{cc}^{++}$

date.quote: A highly significant structure is observed in the Λc+K-π+π+ mass spectrum

key_value_text.quote: the Ξcc++ mass is then determined to be 3621.40±0.72(stat.)±0.27(syst.)±0.14(Λc+) MeV/c2

name: Observation of the doubly charmed baryon Xi_cc++

significance.locator: arXiv:1707.01621 abstract (no single overall significance figure stated)
significance.note: The abstract fetched in this session does not state a single overall significance figure (in sigma) for the observation; left null rather than guessed. The companion 2018 confirmation paper (Xi_cc++ -> Xi_c+ pi+, not written as a separate result here) reports 5.9 sigma for that decay mode specifically.

summary.plain: LHCb found a baryon (a proton-like particle) containing two charm quarks for the first time, a state predicted by the quark model but never confirmed with confidence before.
summary.technical: A highly significant structure in the Λc+K-π+π+ mass spectrum is identified as the weakly decaying doubly charmed baryon Ξcc++; the mass difference m(Ξcc++)-m(Λc+) is measured to be 1334.94±0.72(stat)±0.27(syst) MeV/c^2, giving m(Ξcc++)=3621.40±0.72±0.27±0.14 MeV/c^2.

title: Observation of the Doubly Charmed Baryon Ξcc++
why_it_matters: Baryons with two heavy (charm) quarks test QCD predictions for multi-heavy-quark bound states and were long sought after an earlier, unconfirmed SELEX claim for the related Ξcc+ state; LHCb's high-significance observation established the doubly charmed baryon sector on a firm footing.
